rows.name: AbdomenAtlas 3.0 Mini (= AbdomenAtlas 1.1 images)
rows.count_basis: CT volumes (BDMAP ids), not persons: one person can hold two scans (FLARE, KiTS). All 9,262 volumes of the release are on disk; the census lists 7,649 of them and the ranking counts 7,835 as qualifying.
rows.human_annotation_what: None recorded. The fetch took image_only, so any release masks are not on the grid. No radiologist has read the harvest's level calls.
rows.machine_labels: The data platform's anomaly harvest: TotalSegmentator vertebra masks (labeller B), SPINEPS+VERIDAH masks named by level (labeller A), and a level call combined from the two. 13 tier-1 CTs have no SPINEPS mask.

rows.notes: All 9,262 volumes are on disk (sample index: 9,262 images, none annotated). The census listed 7,649 and the ranking counts 7,835 as qualifying; no record names why the rest were left out, but the census's gates (slice thickness, conversion) are not tier criteria: every volume is an abdominal CT with no human vertebral annotation in the held copy, so all are silver4. The unit is volumes, so the count overstates persons (FLARE and KiTS repeats). 687 CTs are near-duplicate candidates and were not merged. The owner still has to decide on the NC-SA term.
rows.truth_caveats: Abdominal fields: about a third reach T1, and none is recorded to reach C2, so no count from C2 is possible. The harvest's level calls are automatic and unread. 150 volumes are CTSpine1K's MSD-T10 people, who carry expert vertebra masks only in the ctspine1k row.

rows.notes: Every constituent collection has a row of its own, so this umbrella row carries no tier counts. Counted alone, it would be mostly silver4 (abdomen, chest and pelvis fields). rows.expected_if_obtained: 753 whole-body CTs, all gold4 or silver4, since no human vertebral annotation is recorded. In the census's whole-body class about two thirds (about 500) show both lumbosacral references, and that is an upper bound for C2-to-sacrum. So roughly up to 500 gold4 and the rest (at least about 250) silver4. A grid read would decide C2 present, sacrum present and no gap.

rows.name: FluoroCap literature panels
rows.modalities: fluoroscopy and XR plain film as published figure panels (re-encoded reproductions of printed figures), plus YouTube video frames
rows.count_basis: figure panels, not persons: 29,500 PNG panels (data/sources/fluorocap.json counts.panels). No patient key exists: the corpus is keyed by source document, about 1,197 to 1,953 (reproduce sources.json#fluorocap contents.subjects), and 11,446 images sit in 10,233 near-duplicate groups, so persons can be neither counted nor de-duplicated.
rows.human_annotation_what: Most levels come from a caption only: the level the paper's author stated in the figure caption text, which is report-only. human_qc_status reads pending on all 21,603 manifest rows, 0 of 17,486 rows were human-verified, and no reader has read any panel. But about 3.6 percent of the 2,815 Dataset A panels scanned for text carry a printed level label on the image itself (textbook ch. 08 line 116), which is the figure author naming a level on the image, a person's level label by the owner's definition: about 101 panels (estimated, 3.6 percent of 2,815; found by a text scan, not verified by a reader). The rest are tiered as not annotated.
rows.machine_labels: Pseudo labels: decoder placements of the caption level (annotation.status pseudo; MANIFEST.md says pseudo). A screening classifier also called 5,665 of the 18,119 panels scored on 15 September likely spine radiographs and 8,843 not an X-ray at all. These are its calls only: its 93.1 percent accuracy was measured on film-manifest items, not on FluoroCap.
rows.dominant_tier: silver4 (the largest assigned share; by panels, not persons)
rows.licence: the publishers' (figures); per-article licence tiers A to E; figure reuse only, never redistributed
evidence: data/sources/fluorocap.json fields what, level_truth, status, counts.panels
docs/research/data-manifest/MANIFEST.md line 26 (fluorocap 361,567 images, manifest says pseudo) and line 25 (a second, unmapped copy)
docs/textbook/08-fluorocap-as-a-dataset.md lines 26 (Dataset A 2,815 panels passed the E5 screening), 100, 116 (3.6 percent of 2,815 carry a printed level label), 118, 130, 138
rows.truth_caveats: Out of training by directive D1 (2026-09-23); it may serve as a test set at most, and only after a two-reader adjudicated read, which has not begun. Caption levels are estimated to carry 5 to 10 percent counting-convention noise. The record (fluorocap.json what) says 72.8 percent of panels are reproductions with no pixel residual, so they are not native detector frames (chapter 08 declines to quote that share until its script is cited). The tier split rests on a machine classifier's calls, not on verified reads. The about 101 printed-label panels are a text-scan estimate on Dataset A, not a reader's count, and the chapter treats those labels as a leak for training; they are counted as human annotation here because the figure author named the level on the image. Some radiograph panels could be whole-spine films (gold3/gold4 once a read confirms C2 to the sacrum); this is unmeasured.
rows.notes: How the panels were split: silver3 101 (estimated) are the Dataset A panels a text scan found carrying a printed level label, taken out of the classifier's spine-radiograph share since Dataset A passed the E5 screening. silver4 5,564 are the rest of the 5,665 panels the classifier called likely spine radiographs. outside 8,843 are those it called not an X-ray. unknown 14,992 is 3,611 scored panels that fell in neither class plus 11,381 panels never scored (29,500 minus 18,119). The panels and the 21,603-row manifest are not one population: 7,898 panels have no row. The YouTube frames (298,075) are not tiered here and may overlap fluoro_video_clips' YouTube re-encodes.
